Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "1. Executive Architectural Audit Scope and System Topologies
Our distributed real-time media communications network requires an exhaustive architectural evaluation of ICE candidate gathering protocols, STUN server binding sequences, and relay media routing edges across native and web application clients. Under enterprise network configurations characterized by symmetric network address translation, restrictive corporate proxy firewalls, and carrier-grade NAT cellular gateways, media negotiation setup latencies frequently exceed four point two seconds. In worst-case network topologies, peer session negotiation suffers fatal connection establishment failures when dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 candidate pairs fail to resolve within timeout budgets. This technical audit inspects client signaling state machines, protocol message serialization, edge relay allocation topologies, and end-to-end telemetry observability across the media pipeline.

2. Browser Peer Connection Lifecycle and Workspace File Tagging
In client signaling workers, developers must inspect peer connection lifecycle state machines. Tag peer connection dot ts to audit RTCPeerConnection configuration parameters, ensuring that iceTransportPolicy is set to all and bundlePolicy is set to max-bundle. Client routines must attach event handlers to onicecandidate and oniceconnectionstatechange to capture transient network interface transitions. Spoken tag cues must accurately link workspace references to target files during code reviews. Developers must ensure that peer connection teardown routines release audio track buffers and cleanup WebGL video sink pipelines without leaking browser memory allocations during rapid reconnect cycles.

3. Session Description Protocol and Candidate Serialization Routines
Protocol encoding logic implemented in session description dot rs requires strict conformance to RFC 8445 specifications. Tag session description dot rs to inspect candidate attribute parsing for host, server reflexive, and relay candidate types. The parser must validate candidate priority calculation formulas, foundation token uniqueness, and component identification integers without truncating IPv6 address representations. In addition, the serialization harness must gracefully validate candidate transport types, distinguishing between UDP, TCP active, and TCP passive modes while discarding malformed candidate attributes from legacy SIP gateway peers.

4. Distributed TURN Relay Infrastructure Configuration and Credentials
Edge relay instances deployed across geographic regions terminate STUN and TURN allocations under high concurrency. Review turn config dot yaml in the deployment directory to verify authentication mechanisms, shared secret generation, and ephemeral credential lifetimes. The TURN configuration must enforce allocation bandwidth quotas of two megabits per second per stream and configure UDP buffer sizes to sixteen megabytes to prevent packet loss during burst video keyframe transmissions. The relay infrastructure must also balance traffic across diverse regional clusters using geographic DNS Anycast routing while preserving session stickiness during active media calls.

5. Gathering State Machine and Trickle ICE Signaling Optimizations
Traditional WebRTC implementations wait for complete ICE candidate gathering before exchanging SDP offer-answer envelopes, introducing unacceptable call setup latency over mobile cellular connections. The signaling gateway in gateway dot ts must fully implement Trickle ICE. Client endpoints should transmit initial SDP offers immediately following host candidate discovery, streaming subsequent reflexive and relay candidates asynchronously across WebSocket signaling channels. Furthermore, the signaling layer must implement exponential backoff retry schedules for candidate transmission acknowledgments, ensuring that transient network disconnects do not abort ongoing call negotiations.

6. Network Interface Switching, Multi-Homing, and Connection Migration
Mobile client applications frequently transition between cellular radio data and local wireless networks during active voice calls. The media transport coordinator in transport dot rs must support ICE restart sequences and connection migration. When client telemetry detects consecutive packet loss exceeding twenty percent, the engine must trigger an ICE restart without tearing down the underlying media capture pipeline or renegotiating audio codecs. The transport layer should also maintain background probing on dormant candidate pairs to enable zero-interruption failover during physical Wi-Fi disconnections.

7. Security Boundaries, Enterprise Traversal, and DTLS-SRTP Policies
To guarantee enterprise compatibility, the media proxy layer must support TURN over TLS on port four hundred forty-three. Review security policy dot json to confirm that self-signed certificates are rejected, minimum TLS version is restricted to TLS one point three, and ALPN negotiation tokens correctly specify turn. Verify that media payload encryption strictly enforces DTLS-SRTP key exchanges. The security boundary must also enforce certificate thumbprint pinning during peer negotiation and implement strict rate-limiting on unauthenticated STUN binding requests to mitigate distributed denial of service vectors.

8. Telemetry Dashboard, Quality of Experience Metrics, and Audit Sign-Off
Platform site reliability engineers must instrument Prometheus metrics tracking mean gathering duration, ICE failure ratios, and relay fallback percentages. Document all architectural findings in audit report dot md and obtain operational approval from network infrastructure leads before deploying client library updates. The telemetry monitoring system must establish automated alerts triggered when median round-trip times exceed one hundred fifty milliseconds or when audio packet jitter exceeds thirty milliseconds across regional edge aggregates.", "output": "1.
